regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020

official_sources.title: Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020 — Compendium Version II (04.01.2024)
Foods for Infant Nutrition — official amendments register

general_requirements.approval_rule: Infant milk substitutes, infant foods or infant FSMP products without a specified standard require Food Authority approval for the article and its label.
general_requirements.packaging: Use hermetically sealed sound containers/flexible packs compliant with the Packaging Regulations; products are packed under inert atmosphere and packaging for these products shall be BPA-free.
general_requirements.nutrient_tolerance: Minus 10% variation from declared nutrient/nutritional-ingredient values is allowed, while nutrient levels shall not exceed specified maxima.
general_requirements.source_compounds: Use permitted source compounds for minerals, vitamins and other nutrients from the applicable schedules.
general_requirements.dha_ara: DHA/ARA source and level rules apply as specified in the current regulation; DHA claim triggers the stated minimum.
general_requirements.carbohydrate_rule: Lactose and glucose polymers are preferred carbohydrates; sucrose/fructose are restricted as specified.
general_requirements.hydrogenated_fat_rule: Hydrogenated/partially hydrogenated fats are prohibited where the individual standard specifies.
general_requirements.microbiology: Appendix B of the Food Products Standards and Food Additives Regulations applies as specified.
general_requirements.contaminants: Current Contaminants, Toxins and Residues Regulations apply.
general_requirements.promotion: Products are subject to the IMS Act, 1992 as amended, including advertising/marketing restrictions.

7.name: Infant formula
prohibited_or_restricted: Hydrogenated vegetable oils and fats shall not be used.
L(+) lactic acid producing bacteria require prior Food Authority approval.

direct_additive_notes: Limits are expressed per 100 ml product ready for consumption unless otherwise stated.
If more than one of INS 322 and INS 471 is used, the maximum level for each is reduced according to the relative proportion of the other substance.
Schedule I(d) additives for special nutrient formulations may also be used where applicable.

nutrient_requirements.parameter: Ash insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid

nutrient_table_notes: Where only milk protein is used, a factor N × 6.38 may be used.
Lauric acid plus myristic acid shall not exceed 20% of total fatty acids.
Trans fatty acids shall not exceed 3% of total fatty acids.
Erucic acid shall not exceed 1% of total fatty acids.
Total phospholipids shall not exceed 300 mg/100 kcal.

8.name: Milk-cereal based complementary food
core_rules: Based on milk plus cereals and/or legumes/pulses, millets, nuts and permitted protein ingredients.
May contain specified edible vegetable oil, defatted oil-seed extracts, protein concentrates/isolates/hydrolysates, milk solids, carbohydrates, phosphates and citrates.
Hydrogenated vegetable fats and oils shall not be used.

core_composition.condition: For product intended to be mixed with water or milk

fatty_acid_rules: Partially hydrogenated oils and fats shall not be used.

11.name: Food for Infants based on traditional food ingredients
form_rules: May be reconstituted with milk, water, curd or another appropriate medium
11.additives: If required, additives specified for milk-cereal based complementary food may be used.
label_rules: Prominently display 'Traditional Food for Infants' on the front of pack.

12.name: Food for special medical purpose intended for infants
12.composition_rule: Based on sound medical and nutritional principles; except for preterm formula, energy/nutrient composition is based on infant/follow-up formula according to age, modified only as needed for the relevant disease/disorder/medical condition.
12.evidence_rule: Nutritional safety, adequacy and benefit for the intended dietary management shall be scientifically demonstrated.
12.advertising_rule: No food business operator shall advertise infant formula for special medical purpose intended for infants.
12.additives: Use infant-formula/follow-up-formula additive provisions as applicable plus Schedule I(d) special nutrient formulation additives.

13.name: Preterm infant milk substitute
13.age_scope: Babies born before 37 weeks, until 40 weeks gestational age or as prescribed by physician
label_rules: Display 'FOR THE PRETERM BABY (BORN BEFORE 37 WEEKS)' in capital/bold with the product name.
Display the prescribed medical-advice statement in capital and bold.

14.name: Lactose free infant milk substitutes
label_rules: Display 'LACTOSE-FREE' conspicuously in capital and bold letters.
Display 'RECOMMENDED TO BE USED UNDER MEDICAL ADVICE ONLY' in capital and bold letters.
Apply the current lactose-intolerance use/withdrawal statements.

15.name: Hypoallergenic infant milk substitutes
15.protein_rule: Protein shall be extensively hydrolysed whey protein or casein, or the product shall contain only free amino acids.
label_rules: If no milk or milk derivatives are present, conspicuously state 'CONTAINS NO MILK OR MILK PRODUCTS'.
Display 'HYPOALLERGENIC FORMULA' and the prescribed medical-advice statement for products intended for milk-protein-allergic infants.

16.name: Foods for Infants with Inborn Errors of Metabolism (IEM)
16.use_rule: Specific dietary management under medical supervision for an FSSAI-specified IEM condition.
16.composition_rule: Specific modification of proteins, fats or carbohydrates to meet the metabolic condition; nutritional safety and adequacy must be scientifically demonstrated.
16.approval_rule: Products may be manufactured/sold/marketed/imported only for IEM conditions specified by the Food Authority; prior approval applies where the regulation requires.
label_rules: Print 'FOOD FOR SPECIAL MEDICAL PURPOSE' in capital and bold near the product/brand name.
State the specific IEM nutritional-management indication and other prescribed medical-supervision information.

7(3).name: Infant Milk Food
7(3).definition_rule: An infant formula in powder format manufactured without the specific vegetable oil/linoleate/vitamin E/starch/specified additive/optional-ingredient uses described in regulation 7(3) may be named 'Infant Milk Food'.
7(3).foscos_note: FoSCoS currently displays 'Chapter 4(12) of Infant Nutrition Regulations, 2020' for this product; PMSV preserves that catalogue text but links the actual product-name condition in the current compendium to regulation 7(3).
7(3).additive_naming_condition: The 'Infant Milk Food' naming route applies only to the powder-format condition in regulation 7(3), including manufacture without the specified food additive use and optional ingredients described there.

direct_additive_rule: For infant-nutrition products, use the product-specific additive tables in these Regulations first. Do not substitute ordinary-food Appendix A permissions merely because an FCS code exists.
source_compound_rule: Vitamins/minerals/nutrients must use permitted sources under the applicable schedules.
final_compliance_lock: Do not issue final formulation compliance until the complete nutrient table, direct additive table, source-compound schedules, microbiology, contaminants and product-specific label declarations for the selected infant product are machine-normalized.
